knowledge_checks.title: Active Recall: CD-R1
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. In a multiple linear model Y = X beta + epsilon, which statement correctly describes ordinary least squares?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: OLS estimates coefficients by minimising squared differences between observed and fitted responses.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Y is the response, X contains predictors, and OLS minimises residual sum of squares.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Confusing variable roles or minimising fitted values rather than residuals.

choices.label: Y is the response, columns of X are explanatory variables, and OLS chooses beta to minimise the sum of squared residuals.
OLS chooses Y to minimise the sum of squared fitted values.
Every explanatory variable must be independent of every other explanatory variable.
Multiple regression fits a separate response for each predictor.

knowledge_checks.title: Revision Checkpoint: residual diagnostics under heteroscedasticity
knowledge_checks.prompt: Closed-book. An OLS fit has residuals whose spread increases markedly with fitted values. What is the best interpretation?
hints: Use the concept from this learning objective only.
knowledge_checks.explanation: A funnel-shaped residual plot indicates heteroscedasticity, which affects usual OLS inference.
knowledge_checks.model_answer: Investigate non-constant variance and consider a justified transformation, variance model, or robust inference.
knowledge_checks.common_mistake: Treating high R-squared as a substitute for residual diagnostics.

choices.label: The constant-variance assumption is doubtful, so usual standard errors and inference may be unreliable without an appropriate remedy.
The pattern proves the fitted mean relationship is exactly correct.
The pattern is harmless whenever R-squared is high.
Always remove observations with the largest residuals.
